envelope: v1 unchanged: {v:1, id, method, params}; deny_unknown_fields everywhere; protocol_version 1
status_in_wp0: Every added method parses and validates its params, then answers NOT_IMPLEMENTED (before opening storage) until its WP lands. Removed methods still parse until WP1 moves them behind the legacy-tasks feature, after which they answer UNKNOWN_METHOD in the default build.

kept_notes.hello: the supervisor field of its result is retired with the task pipeline (WP1)
kept_notes.pet.pause: kept in the protocol; no UI ('Going away' removed, Off covers it)
kept_notes.pet.rules: also backs the Help Hardcore switch: permadeath->gentle any time; gentle->permadeath only with acknowledgement, the optional param confirm_name (raw input <= 256 bytes, not blank, no NUL) matching the pet's name after core normalize_pet_name, as pet.retire (INVALID_PARAMS otherwise), and a healthy pet (INVALID_STATE -> 'Make {name} happy first.'). confirm_name is ignored for every other change and kept out of the receipt digest when absent (WP1)
kept_notes.state.get: may migrate; first drains the inbox (fold.lock LOCK_NB, at most one batch); snapshot adds enabled, count_helpers, agent, clients, treats; drops active_task, recent, providers, settings, decay, care.ready_to_work, care.readiness_reasons (WP1); schema_version 5

name.description: raw input <= 256 bytes, not blank, no NUL; content rule is core normalize_pet_name (1..=24 chars, <= 96 bytes) -> NAME_INVALID

added.semantics: One transaction. No living life -> adopt (pace steady). Living unarmed life -> select look, rename if a name is given, set rules with pet.rules semantics, arm. Then spend the welcome routine if welcome_care_available. life_id, when given, must name the living life (NOT_FOUND otherwise). While Off: INVALID_STATE (the picker shows Turn on instead of Let's go!).

name.description: raw input <= 256 bytes, not blank, no NUL; content rule is core normalize_pet_name (1..=24 chars, <= 96 bytes) -> NAME_INVALID

added.semantics: Living lives only. Name validated in Rust (core normalize_pet_name) before the UPDATE, so the lives.name CHECK never fires.

Gives one treat: marks the oldest unspent activity_turns row given and inserts one activity_xp row (5 XP) in the same transaction, then journals evolution. PET_NEEDS_CARE while asleep, paused or fainted. While Off: INVALID_STATE.

SPEC §7.3. Off: settle presence and sleep up to now, meta.enabled=0, commit, create $STATE/off (0600), export enabled:false + presence.wanted:false. On: enabled=1, remove the flag, export; no catch-up. Idempotent; works with no living life.
Sets meta.count_helpers and creates/removes $STATE/helpers (read by the shim).

SPEC §5.10. Deletes agent_events and agent_sessions; sets activity_turns.earned_at_ms to 0, except that an earn from the last 24 h keeps ceil_hour(earned_at_ms) + 1 ms (marked, cleared to 0 once it leaves the day, so the treat caps stay durable; notes.md §7 item 1), and sets given_at_ms of given rows to 0 (unspent rows stay unspent). Unspent treats and earned XP stay. Takes fold.lock (LOCK_NB, BUSY if held) before the DB.

result.clients: array, one entry per supported client in client order: {id, name, installed, version, connected, needs_step, last_seen_ms, first_seen_ms, events_7d, job, failed_reason}

added.semantics: File-only (<= 50 ms): never runs a client binary, no network. Writes client_hooks and re-exports. events_7d = COUNT(agent_events) for the client in the last 7 days (not a column).
added.receipt_note: Deliberately no receipt (notes.md section 2): it is a file-only re-check whose answer must reflect the files now; replaying a stored answer under the same request id would show stale status. It is idempotent.

added.semantics: Returns {job_id} at once; a detached `codepet clients-job` does the work (SPEC §5.2). This click is the consent. TEST_STATE while the bar runs with a stateHome test override. While Off: INVALID_STATE (the ready check could only fail, because the shim exits on the off flag).
Detached job: writes $STATE/clients/<id>.disconnected first, then removes exactly CodePet's artifact (Codex: tombstone rule). Allowed while Off (uninstall disconnects every client).

The ready check, as a detached job: sets meta.test_state running (test_at_ms, test_client = the first tested client in client order), writes a fresh $STATE/test.nonce (0600, 32 lowercase hex), and runs each tested connected client's exact stored command string (commands.json) with its ready_check payloads carrying codepet_test=<nonce>: turn_start, then turn_done test_done_delay_ms later. The hook compares the nonce; the fold keeps test records only while running and never changes test_state. The job sets done when every tested client's turn_done record arrived within test_done_delay_ms + test_arrival_ms, else failed (those clients get last_reason ready_check), removes the nonce and exports. Test events never update last_seen_ms, first_seen_ms, events_7d or sessions, and never earn. TEST_STATE under a stateHome test override (the stored commands point at the real state dir). While Off: INVALID_STATE.

error_codes_added.NAME_INVALID: pet.start / pet.rename name fails normalize_pet_name; UI 'That name is too long.'
error_codes_added.PET_NEEDS_CARE: treats.give while asleep, paused or fainted
error_codes_added.TEST_STATE: clients.connect / clients.disconnect / clients.test while the bar runs with a stateHome test override

added.migrate: explicit migration (installer); WP1. Migration ownership (SPEC §6.2): only `codepet migrate` and `codepet rpc` state.get upgrade an older database; `codepet state` (which prints the current snapshot) and every other command refuse one untouched with SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED ('needs `codepet migrate`'). A brand-new state directory is an install, not a migration: any opening command creates it at schema 5, without a companion
added.fold --state-dir <abs> [--lock-fd N]: internal; safe by hand (takes the lock itself without --lock-fd); WP2
added.clients-job <job_id>: internal detached Connect/Disconnect/test job; job_id must match job_id_pattern; WP3
added.connect [--repoint] [id...|--all] / disc: wrappers for clients.*; wait for the job and print plain words; WP3. --all = every installed supported client that is not connected and has no running job, except codex (the UI's Connect all); Codex only when named: `codepet connect codex`. Ids are the client ids; anything else exits 2 with the usage line. Refused while Off (off_behaviour). Post-freeze (notes.md section 10 item 16): `--repoint` (first, with named ids, never --all) lets this Connect repoint a hook shim that serves another existing state dir or binary (otherwise blocked). `disconnect <id>` for an app with no CodePet files that is not connected prints '<name>: CodePet is not connected there; nothing to stop', exits 0 and records nothing
added.clients-refresh: internal (installer step 7), post-freeze (notes.md section 10 item 2): refreshes connected clients' wholly CodePet-owned files whose marker is present and whose bytes differ, and upgrades an older shim in place with its own S/B; never runs a client and never edits a shared file; WP3
added.doctor [--json]: plain words, changes nothing; --json stable and never includes config contents; WP3

cli.wp0_behaviour: added commands other than hook print 'NOT_IMPLEMENTED: codepet <cmd> is not implemented yet in this v0.3 build' on stderr and exit 1 without touching state; hook exits 0 silently

job_id_rule: 'job-' + 24 lowercase hex (12 bytes from sys::random_bytes). It names the journal $STATE/jobs/<job_id>.json and appears in the export, so nothing else is ever accepted as a job id (the clients-job subcommand refuses any other argument).

clients.status.description: Exactly five entries, one per supported client, in client order. Every field except name, events_7d and the per-id order is also the export's clients.<id> entry (bar.v2.schema.json $defs/client). events_7d follows agent_vectors.json fold.events_7d. Fixtures: fixtures/clients-status/*.json

snapshot_v03.description: state.get (and every method that returns the snapshot) in v0.3. Only the v0.3 changes are frozen here; the rest of the v0.2 snapshot is unchanged. The agent, treats and clients blocks have exactly the bar.v2 shape (the same Rust structs serialise both). WP1 fills enabled/count_helpers/treats/lifecycle, WP2 agent, WP3 clients.

frozen_reason_precedence.rule: the first that applies: no living life -> no_life; meta.enabled = 0 -> off; death_pending -> pending; not armed -> unarmed; pet.pause -> paused; a slot task (legacy-tasks only; never in the default build) -> task; asleep -> sleeping; else none. presence.wanted = enabled and armed and not paused and not death_pending (and no slot task)

snapshot_v03.checked_by: check_contracts.py builds a snapshot from each bar-v2 fixture's blocks and validates it against this schema

off_behaviour.rule: While meta.enabled = 0 a refused method answers INVALID_STATE (message 'CodePet is off') before it changes anything; an allowed method runs normally and settlement discards the Off time (no decay, grace, XP or death). Refusal is checked inside the method's transaction, after receipt replay.

why.clients.connect|clients.test: the shim exits on the off flag, so the ready check could only fail
why.clients.disconnect: uninstall disconnects every client and must work while Off
why.pet.care|pet.sleep|pet.wake|pet.pause|pe: the Off look offers only Turn on; nothing may age, arm, grow or end a life while Off

cli.connect: refused: prints 'CodePet is off. Turn it on first: codepet on' and exits 1
